newsitem.title: WESTERN SAMOA: Pacific Islands back environmental action plan.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Islands back environmental action plan.

text.p: Thirteen Pacific island nations have teamed up to create a joint action programme to protect and develop the region's international waters.
The project is intended to improve coastal and ocean resources management covering areas such as fish stocks, tourism development, protection of water supplies and pollution control.
Representatives launched the initiative, known as the Strategic Action Programme for International Waters of the Pacific region, at a meeting in Apia last week, officials said.

Finance for the project will be raised by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), which is managed by the World Bank and United Nations, with contributions from the Australian and New Zealand governments.

"This is the first GEF project specifically addressing the international waters focal area in the (Pacific) region," Tamarii Tutangata, director of the South Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP) said in a statement.
He said it was also "the first in the world for the design of a strategic action programme in international waters for a group of small island developing states."
A regional task force will spend the next three months drawing up the action programme, having held their first meeting last week at SPREP headquarters in Apia.

Anthony Patten, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) resident representative in Apia, said the role of the core group of five nations, non-governmental organisations and private sector and GEF-linked agencies involved in the task force would be crucial.
"I personally believe that the success of the project will hinge largely on the work of this regional task force in guiding the direction the project ought to take," he said.
The thrust of the plan is part of a worldwide drive to protect vital ecosystems across rich and poor nations by supporting environmentally-sustainable development and conservation programmes.
